Carotenoids as pro-oxidants
Although at low oxygen pressure, carotenoids act as a chain breaking antioxidants, at high oxygen pressure they are readily autoxi-
dized and exhibit pro-oxidant activity. With higher concentrations of oxygen, the carotenoid radical (Car$) may react with dioxygen

(O2) forming a carotenoid peroxyl radical (Car-OO$) (auto-oxidation). These radicals act as pro-oxidants as they cause lipid (LH)
peroxidation and promote oxidative damage in other biomolecules (e.g., DNA, proteins). Hydrophobic lipid (LOO$) may react
with carotenoids to produce oxidation products that will be further metabolized and eliminated from the body (Ribeiro et al.,
2018).
Effects of storage and processing
Carotenoids are susceptible to oxidative degradation and isomerization resulting from storage and processing conditions (Dias
et al., 2021). These reactions result in both loss of color and biological activity and formation of unpleasant volatile compounds.
